questions: How many nano-SQUIDs did you measure in total, including those with one or no working tunnel probe, and how many showed the Ic oscillations, the diode sign reversal, the spectral jumps and zero-bias peaks?
Why were the other devices set aside, beyond the tunnel-junction yield you mention ("below 50%", p. 5)?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: Bx above 4 T for devices B and C, VG beyond ±30 V, field angle, and temperature?

What does the second-best device or dataset look like, in particular any other first-generation single-probe device, and the device A data where the zero-bias peak did not appear at the diode reversal?

What are the tunnel resistances of each junction in devices A, B and C? Figs. S1 and S2b show local conductance of about 1 e^2/h (about 26 kΩ) and above, while the Methods say the contacts "typically exhibit resistances exceeding 100 kΩ" (p. 5). Was any filter or line resistance subtracted from the local conductance, and how was the preamplifier offset that sets zero bias corrected (per trace or once per dataset)?

For the end-to-end correlation (Figs. 4c,f,i,l and S3), what smoothing and bias step did you use for the third derivative, was there a threshold below which a curvature counts as neither peak nor dip, and how does the "strong increase of correlated zero-bias conductance peaks" in device C (Suppl. p. 5) fit with "a zero-bias conductance peak was mostly absent in this device" (Suppl. p. 4)?
In the zero-field gate maps (Fig. 4a-b), do the zero-bias peaks follow Coulomb-diamond-like or even-odd patterns, and how do they change with temperature?

Does the sign pattern of η in Bx (Fig. S4) mirror when the back gate changes the top-bottom asymmetry, and how does a trivial asymmetric two-junction interferometer model with your measured parameters compare with Figs. 1e and 3a?
